blocks.text: GENEVA, Switzerland—Net food-importing countries such as the Philippines should keep food trade open while strengthening food security measures to cushion supply disruptions, according to the World Trade Organization’s (WTO) top official. Speaking to foreign journalists here, WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala said these countries should still adopt domestic food security measures to feed their populations. READ: WTO worries about food security in Southeast Asia She mentioned that certain WTO member countries maintain food stocks that they can use during emergencies as part of a broader food security agenda. “You need appropriate domestic policies that are not really protectionist.
